scenario_text: An NBFC wants to build an AI-based credit risk scoring engine but they're not sure exactly what data sources to use or what the model architecture should look like. There's significant technical risk — they've never built ML systems before. Budget is uncertain and depends on initial results. They want to build a proof of concept first before committing to full development.

requirements.statement: The system shall be capable of integrating with multiple external data sources for credit risk assessment
requirements.business_justification: Access to diverse data sources is crucial for building accurate credit risk models
requirements.assumptions: Data sources are available and can be integrated via APIs or data dumps
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can successfully ingest and process data from at least three external sources
applicable_regulations: Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks (including RRBs) and AIFIs §3.3 (RBI/2024-25 Fraud Risk Management) [revised 2024]

requirements.statement: The system shall support multiple machine learning model architectures for credit risk scoring
requirements.business_justification: Different models may be more suitable for different data sources or problem domains
requirements.assumptions: Model architectures are well-defined and can be implemented
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can successfully train and deploy at least two different model architectures

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user-friendly interface for data scientists to configure and monitor model performance
requirements.business_justification: Easy-to-use interfaces increase productivity and reduce errors
requirements.assumptions: Data scientists have basic knowledge of ML and data science tools
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Interface allows for easy configuration of model hyperparameters and monitoring of performance metrics

requirements.statement: The system shall be capable of generating a proof of concept within a reasonable timeframe (e.g., 3-6 months)
requirements.business_justification: Proof of concept is necessary to demonstrate feasibility and secure funding
requirements.assumptions: Resources (people, budget) are allocated for the proof of concept phase
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System generates a functional proof of concept within the specified timeframe

requirements.statement: The system shall be developed with a modular architecture to facilitate future scalability and maintenance
requirements.business_justification: Modular architecture reduces technical debt and makes it easier to add new features
requirements.assumptions: Development team has experience with modular architecture
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System can be easily scaled and maintained without significant rework

sdlc.shortcut: High technical uncertainty + proof of concept required + user-friendly interface -> Prototype
sdlc.cross_check_reasoning: Agile fits because it allows for iterative development, rapid delivery, and flexibility to adapt to changing requirements, which is suitable for high-priority requirements like integrating with external data sources and generating a proof of concept within a reasonable timeframe. Incremental also fits because it allows for phased development, which is suitable for high-priority requirements like supporting multiple machine learning model architectures and developing a modular architecture to facilitate future scalability and maintenance.
